distractors.reason: A 'letter' is a longer written message sent by post. We don't say 'greeting letter' for a short card with good wishes.
A 'book' is a bound set of pages to read. We don't say 'greeting book' for a card.
A 'photo' is a picture taken with a camera. We don't say 'greeting photo' for a card with wishes written on it.

example_sentence: My aunt sent me a colorful greeting ___ on my birthday.
l1_interference: Osoby mówiące po polsku mogą zmienić kolejność rzeczowników i powiedzieć 'card greeting' zamiast poprawnego 'greeting card', ponieważ w języku angielskim pierwszy rzeczownik określa drugi.
explanation: In English compound nouns, the first noun describes the type of the second one. A 'greeting card' is a type of card, so 'greeting' comes first.

related_collocations.example: I bought a birthday card for my best friend.
She made a phone call to say hello.
We will meet at the bus stop at eight.

memory_tip: The FIRST noun names the TYPE of the SECOND noun: a GREETING card, a BUS stop, a PHONE call.
